PAINTING OF SPANISH BLAURY FOR N. HIGH
$5,000 WAS ILL USED.

Gitana, Spanish Gypsy, one of the most beautiful women in Spain, painted by Rafael Sanchis Yago, Spanish artist and friend of King Alfonso of Spain. The Spanish King has said of him "Spanish Art could not find a better and more dignified interpreter than yourself". Yago has been offered as much as $5,000 for this portrait, but has turned every offer down. He has painted many wonderful types of Spanish and Southamerican women, and has come to this country to paint some of America's beauties. He works in sepia with a little coloring. This portrait with many of his other masterpieces are on exhibition at Kennedy's Galleries. 11/24/22

GREATEST MATADOR, SLAYER OF 2,000 BULLS, COMING TO U.S.
TO VISIT GREATEST ARTIST WHO PAINTED THIS PICTURE.

S/372,732 Belmonte," champion matador," as painted by Ygnacio Zuloaga, the famous Spanish artist who is now in this country for his first visit," in his ring costume of golden yellow satin embroidered in gold.

Still under 30, Belmonte has slain more than 2,000 $k$ bulls," earning a fortune of about a million dollars and the reputation of greatest living bullfighter. He lives in princessly style and has educated himself to enjoy the company of writers," painters, sculptors," musicians and other artists with whom he," as chief exponent of the art of the torro; consorts.

He is now in Peru," filling a two months engagement," and is soon to come to New York to see his old friend, Zuloaga(who is also noted as a matador--amateur) and to be feted by the Spanish colony in New York," members of which plan to give him a great banquet to which leaders of all branches of sport will be invited.
